paper.title_en: Role of nuclear shell effects of various nuclear physics ingredients in shaping <math><mi>r</mi></math>-process abundance patterns
paper.abstract_en: Nuclear shell effects play a crucial role in shaping the solar <math><mi>r</mi></math>-process abundance pattern, while the individual contributions of shell effects in various nuclear physics ingredients, including nuclear masses, <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay rates, and neutron-capture rates, remain insufficiently understood. We systematically investigate the influence of the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> shells on the final abundances, particularly the shell effects of three nuclear physics ingredients. Our results demonstrate that removing the nuclear shell effects disrupts key features of the <math><mi>r</mi></math>-process abundance distribution, causing the material to become almost uniformly distributed over a mass range of roughly <math><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math> units. In addition, the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> shells exhibit opposite effects on the production of heavy nuclei with <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>></mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math>. We further find that the propagation of shell-structure changes to nuclear masses has the largest impact on the final abundances, followed by neutron-capture rates. In contrast, within the simplified diagnostic tests adopted here, shell-related discontinuities in <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay rates at magic numbers have only a minor direct influence on the resulting abundance pattern. In addition to magic shells, relativistic mean field (RMF) models predict the presence of spurious shells at <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>58</mn></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>92</mn></mrow></math>. We find that an artificial increase of 1 MeV in nuclear binding energy at <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>92</mn></mrow></math> produces a pronounced enhancement of abundances around <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>140</mn></mrow></math>, potentially altering the overall abundance pattern, whereas the <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>58</mn></mrow></math> spurious shell has only a minor effect, causing merely a small change near the <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>155</mn></mrow></math> region.
